descriptionChirho: Active intensive covering of a surface, object, or person with a physical material such as a cloth, cloud, skin, or earth (Arabic ghatta / yughattiyi).
Concealing information, sin, or wrongdoing from knowledge; keeping secret or veiling from sight (Arabic satara, katama, akhfa).
Covering a person specifically with garments or clothing, often as an act of care or honor (Arabic kasa).
Waters, darkness, or shame covering and overwhelming a person or place, submerging them entirely (Arabic ghashiya, ghamara).
Passive state of being covered, veiled, or submerged, whether by physical material or metaphorical force (Pual, Niphal, and Qal passive participle forms).
Reflexive self-covering with a garment, veil, or sackcloth, whether for mourning, modesty, or disguise (Arabic taghatta, iktasa).
